newsitem.title: USA: Dole to campaign around-the-clock to election day.
newsitem.headline: Dole to campaign around-the-clock to election day.

text.p: Republican presidential challenger Bob Dole, in a dramatic move to try to overcome President Bill Clinton's wide lead in the polls, announced on Thursday that he will campaign around-the-clock starting Friday for four days until election day

"The last time I fought round the clock for my country was in 1945 in Italy," Dole said in reference to his service in World War II. He made the announcement in remarks prepared for a campaign speech in Miami.
Dole said the trip would last 96 hours, starting at 12 noon EST (1700 GMT) on Friday.
"I am determined to make every hour of this decisive election count." Dole said. "The stakes are that high."
Dole campaign spokesman Nelson Warfield said the trip would be by bus, plane and other transport and would end in the state with the most electoral votes, California.

All opinion polls show Clinton leading Dole by a comfortable margin. The Reuters tracking poll on Thursday put Clinton ahead by 7.7 points, and a new poll in California showed Clinton leading by 18 points.
